subject.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue

question: Should this PR implement true starvation prevention where aged low-priority work may overtake fresh foreground work, or should OpenClaw keep foreground-preserving one-tier aging and leave the stronger starvation request tracked elsewhere?
rationale: Both policies are plausible but have different user-visible scheduling tradeoffs; automation can repair the helper drift only after maintainers choose the intended scheduler contract.

options.title: Implement true bounded aging
options.body: Aged low-priority entries may overtake fresh foreground work after the threshold, matching the canonical starvation issue and the PR's original proof claim.

options.title: Keep foreground-preserving aging
options.body: The branch can keep one-tier promotion, but it must update claims and avoid closing the canonical starvation request as solved.

options.title: Pause for broader scheduler work
options.body: The branch can wait or close in favor of the broader gateway/queue fairness policy if maintainers want one combined scheduler design.

recommendation.title: Implement true bounded aging
recommendation.body: Aged low-priority entries may overtake fresh foreground work after the threshold, matching the canonical starvation issue and the PR's original proof claim.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced and hardened the command queue and authored an overlapping scheduler-priority branch, making them the best available routing owner for the policy choice.
